assumptions.statement: Supplier B's stoppage record of the last three years (two force-majeure stoppages, 9 and 14 days) repeats over the 2026-2028 commitment, and with 100% of volume on Supplier B each stoppage costs the full gross margin quoted in the supply risk review
assumptions.rationale: Only history available; the incumbent can cover up to 60% of volume but only at two weeks' notice, so a 9-14 day stoppage is largely uncovered. Two events is a small sample: a single stoppage of 14 days (2.4 EUR M) would not by itself erase the full move's 2.93 EUR M advantage.
assumptions.validate: Supplier B force-majeure root causes and business-continuity plan, before contract signature

assumptions.statement: Price-eligible spend splits in line with the 70/30 volume split, so 9% applies to 70% and 4% to 30% of the 23.9 EUR M
assumptions.rationale: 2025 invoices excluding rush freight split 16.7 / 7.2 EUR M between incumbent and Supplier B, i.e. 70/30

assumptions.statement: Rush freight is caused by our own forecast errors and is not removed by changing supplier; neither offer reduces it
assumptions.rationale: Invoice notes flag the high-freight months as 'rush freight passed through: our forecast errors'; finance states the unit-price reduction does not apply to it
